findings.reason: §3's done-when turns on a token figure, so the plan must either extend the existing transcript/token reader or state in its text why a separate reader is required, before the rewrite node is dispatched.
findings.text: the module's own docstring describes per-request input accounting as `input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens` and reads coordinator transcripts under `~/.claude/projects`, both of which reckon/velocity.py already implements in `transcript_index` (:1319) and its token accumulation (:1395–:1401), and which reckon/crew/metering.py derives for run streams; the plan's §3 text names none of them

findings.reason: the reviewer's job is to name the owner to extend, and extending velocity.py to expose a pre-dispatch skill-load figure is cheaper and keeps one accounting path instead of two that will drift.
findings.text: measure.py is a second reader of the same coordinator transcripts and the same three input-token fields that velocity.py already reads and sums, and it independently computes a median where velocity.py carries a distribution helper; the owning mechanism is reckon/velocity.py (`transcript_index`, token accumulation, distribution) and the plan re-implements it under docs/research/data/

findings.reason: a plan whose evidence rests on nine ad-hoc counters cannot be re-run or reviewed by a third party without re-deriving the whole pipeline, and naming one module with a small interface is exactly the depth the review exists to require.
findings.text: the classification machine is split across scan_binding.py, reconcile_coverage.py, render_dispositions.py, the other-references dir's sentence_counts.py, rows.py and render.py, the reconcile dir's reconcile_skill.py, and the baseline dir's measure.py and figure.py: nine scripts, no exported record type, no single entry point; a reader wanting "the classification of file X" must run a script under one figure dir and match its stdout in another

findings.reason: importing the counter's `sentences_with_lines` and `clean` would remove a subprocess boundary, a duplicated tokeniser, and a stdout format that is itself an untested interface.
findings.text: this script invokes scan_binding.py through `subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(SCAN)])`, parses the counter's stdout with a regex, and on line 25 defines its own `tokens()` tokeniser to compare against the fragment; it is a wrapper over the counter that re-implements the counter's normalisation rather than importing it, and the plan states no reason the counter could not be an importable module

findings.reason: the plan should extend one owner (scan_binding.py's tokeniser, or a shared module it imports) so the §3 word-count and the §2 sentence counts cannot disagree about what a sentence is.
findings.text: `sentences()` here and `sentences_with_lines()` at scan_binding.py:67 are two independent implementations of the same method (drop fenced blocks and headings, neutralise list markers and table pipes, protect the same abbreviation set, split on sentence-final punctuation) written a directory apart for the same plan; §3's word-count gate will need a third caller of it

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the §2 evidence machinery is spread across nine scripts in five directories under docs/figures/the-crew-contract-fits-one-read/, each re-deriving markdown sentence splitting or row parsing, so no module hides the record shape, the store and the join.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the same sentence tokeniser is duplicated between scan_binding.py and sentence_counts.py; the plan should name one owner to extend rather than fork a third copy for §3's word-count gate.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — the plan is a documentation rewrite; it adds no CLI option, no MCP view and no refusal family, and §3's rewrite retires prose (rows marked delete-as-enforced) rather than adding interface surface, so there is nothing for its sections to retire or merge against the supplied counts.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's §3 token-spend measure re-accounts coordinator-transcript input tokens without citing the token accounting and transcript reader that already exist in reckon/velocity.py and reckon/crew/metering.py.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — reconcile_coverage.py shells out to scan_binding.py and re-parses its stdout, wrapping the counter instead of extending it, and re-implements the counter's tokeniser inline; the plan never states why the counter cannot be an imported module.
